sources.role: official source archive; configuration, input, snapshot and ROM implementation (digest measured from downloaded archive)

paths.path: /etc/atari++/atari++.conf, then ~/.atari++.conf, then ./.atari++.conf; -config <file> loads an additional explicit configuration file.
paths.naming: One option per line with `option = value` (leading dash omitted); later files and command-line options override earlier values.

Digital Atari ports use `Joystick.<0..3>.Port = <device>` and sensitivity. Safe Linux kernel input uses `AnalogJoystick.<0..7>` (reads /dev/input/jsN, axes HAxis/VAxis, First_Button through Fourth_Button); SDL builds additionally expose SDLAnalog/SDLDigital with SDL_* axis/button keys. The source does not provide stable device identity beyond the numeric js unit.
evidence: source:machine.cpp constructs four joystick ports and AnalogJoystick/SDLAnalog devices @atari++_1.85
docs:atari++.man JOYSTICK, ANALOGJOYSTICK and SDLANALOG sections

paths.path: Guest saves are written inside mounted writable ATR/ATX/XFD/DCM and other disk/tape images; the emulator has no universal per-game sidecar save directory.
paths.naming: The mounted image keeps its own filename; read-only/protected image status controls write-back.
evidence: source:diskdrive.cpp image open/write paths and protection status @atari++_1.85
docs:http://www.xl-project.com/about.html supported image and save behavior

paths.path: Machine snapshots are explicitly selected through the save requester or `-state <file>` for loading; the menu's default save/load name is `atari++.state`.
paths.naming: Plain text Atari++ snapshot generated by SnapShotWriter, beginning with its `#Atari++ generated snapshot file` header; arbitrary filename is accepted.

paths.path: Built-in OS++ and Basic++ ROM emulation is the default fallback. Optional external images use OsAPath, OsBPath, Os1200Path, OsXLPath, Os5200Path and BasicAPath/BasicBPath/BasicCPath options.
paths.naming: The distribution documents atariosa.rom, atariosb.rom and atarixl.rom in a `roms` directory; no canonical checksum is published.
evidence: docs:README.Compile built-in ROM fallback and roms/ filenames

paths.path: No separate cryptographic key file is required.
paths.naming: No key filename/checksum is published by upstream.
evidence: source:atari++_1.85 has configuration, ROM and snapshot inputs but no key store

paths.path: The source uses `%HOME%/.atari++.conf` and `./.atari++.conf`, plus /etc/atari++/atari++.conf when available; `-config <file>` loads an explicit file.
paths.naming: `option = value` lines; later configuration and command-line options override earlier ones.
Same `Joystick.<n>.Port`, AnalogJoystick/SDLAnalog device and axis/button option grammar as Linux. The source's numeric SDL/Linux device units are not stable identity; no automatic remap is claimed.

paths.path: Inside mounted writable disk/tape images; no universal sidecar save directory.
User-selected snapshot file; default menu basename `atari++.state`, with `-state <file>` for loading.
paths.naming: Plain text Atari++ snapshot with SnapShotWriter header; arbitrary filename.

paths.path: Built-in OS++/Basic++ fallback or external OsAPath/OsBPath/Os1200Path/OsXLPath/Os5200Path and BasicAPath/BasicBPath/BasicCPath images.
paths.naming: Upstream documents atariosa.rom/atariosb.rom/atarixl.rom in roms; no canonical user-ROM checksum.

paths.path: No separate key file is required.

linux-flatpak.reason: The official Atari++ site publishes a source archive and Windows binary but no official Flatpak application.

macos.reason: The official site does not publish a macOS binary or a host-specific macOS configuration/package contract for Atari++ 1.85.
